regions.text: 理由なく「偶然に異理の中へ落ちる」場合を消極的偶然の例として擧げた。

quote.translation: Earlier we gave as an example of negative contingency the case of "falling by chance into the truth" without any ground.

regions.text: その場合、理由の非存在が消極的に目警されてゐるのであるが、「眞理の中へ落ちる」といふ以上はそこに何箏かの相對性が潜んでるなければならない。

quote.translation: In that case the non-existence of a ground is witnessed negatively, but insofar as we say that one "falls into the truth", some relativity must lie hidden there.

regions.text: 節ち一方には兵理の認識といふ理由歸結の必然約開係の系列があら他方には肯定否定の自由意志の必然開係の系列があつて、雨系列間に必然的ならざる相對的開係が成立する限りに於て、兵理が積極偶然として浮出てゐるのである。

quote.translation: On the one side, that is, there is the series of necessary relations of ground and consequent that we call the knowledge of truth; on the other, there is the series of necessary relations of the free will that affirms or denies; and insofar as a non-necessary relative relation holds between the two series, truth emerges as a positive contingency.

regions.text: それ故に舞理の成立に對して認識理由を鋏くといふ滑極偶然の根柢には、認識理由を鋏いてるながら意志決定の系列が眞理認識の系列の中へ落ち込んだといふ積極的偶然が存してるるのである。

quote.translation: At the root of the negative contingency of lacking a ground of knowledge for the truth that is reached, there consequently lies the positive contingency that the series of the will's decisions, though lacking a ground of knowledge, fell into the series of the knowledge of truth.

regions.text: 認識理由を餃いてゐるのであるからその意志決定の系列は誤認の成立してゐる論理的系列の中へ落ち込むことも出来たのである。

quote.translation: Lacking a ground of knowledge, that series of decisions could just as well have fallen into a logical series in which error holds.

regions.text: 兵理といふ積極な存在は二つの獨立した系列が偶然的開係に置かれたところに忽然として浮き上つて來たものである。

quote.translation: The positive existence we call truth is something that suddenly floated up where two independent series were placed in a contingent relation.

regions.text: 目約々消極約偶然の根柢に積極約偶然の溶んでゐることに競ては、「反目的」の場合に開しては、他の關係に於て既に逃べて置いた（三入買参照）。

quote.translation: That positive contingency lies hidden at the root of negative teleological contingency, too, I have already discussed in another connection, with regard to the case of "counter-purpose" (see p. 138).

regions.text: すなばち質現さるべき目的が

quote.translation: When a purpose that ought to be realised is not realised, that is, a purpose that in most cases is realised fails, in that case in particular, to be realised, and for this we could not but think some positive causal contingency on the reverse side.
